newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Clerides says Turkey holds key to missile crisis.
newsitem.headline: Clerides says Turkey holds key to missile crisis.

text.p: Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides offered on Friday to cancel controversial plans to buy Russian anti-aircraft missiles if Ankara agreed a deal on the future of the divided island.
"Of course, we don't want to waste the money," he said in answer to a question at a news conference.

The Cypriot government's decision to buy the missiles has heightened tensions between the island's Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities and between Athens and Ankara. Turkey has threatened to take whatever action is needed to block their deployment.
Clerides, who was attending the World Economic Forum, said that the missiles would in any case not be deployed for at least 18 months.
The veteran leader urged the international community to bring greater pressure to bear on Turkey to reach agreement on the island where the two communities have been partitioned for over 20 years.
The European Union should make it clear to Ankara that its hopes for eventually joining the economic bloc were dependent on resolving the problem of Cyrpus.

(A solution) requires a concerted action by the United States, the Europeans, to convince Turkey that if it continues to occupy that part of Cyprus...you cannot be accepted (into the European Union)," Clerides said.
They have to "pass a clear message to Turkey that you have to solve the Cyprus problem," he said.
Turkey invaded the north of the island in 1974 in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece. The Turkish Cypriot state proclaimed there is recognised only by Ankara.
The Cyprus government has proposed a federalist state in which both communities would have a high degree of autonomy.

U.N. special representative for Cyprus Han Sung-joo of South Korea is in Cyprus on a week-long visit aimed at preparing the ground for a face-to-face meeting between Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
But Clerides said that he did not know when the meeting would take place.
